findings.title: Caller name wrong in design prose
findings.where: design.md path 1b and v3 resolution log
findings.problem: Design calls the sole caller of updateAccuracyCheck 'handleUpdate'; the actual function in app/accuracy-compare/page.tsx is 'handleUpdateCheck'. The call-graph conclusion (one caller, passes xmlAnalyst/fileNameMaster/tolerance) is correct; only the name is wrong.
findings.fix: Replace 'handleUpdate' with 'handleUpdateCheck' in the two places it appears.

findings.title: Update fallback trigger condition vs. what the real caller passes
findings.problem: Fallback fires on 'input.xmlAnalyst === undefined', but the verified sole caller passes 'analyst?.raw ?? null' (null, never undefined) when no analyst is loaded, so a null analyst would skip the stored-row fallback and go straight to the null-grade marker. This is the correct behaviour (handleUpdateCheck guards on !gradedAnalyst), but the prose describes the fallback as covering a 'partial update omitting xmlAnalyst', which a null (not undefined) value would not trigger.
findings.fix: Keep '=== undefined' and add one sentence that a null analyst XML is treated as a genuine ungradeable row (null-grade marker), not a partial update; or widen to 'input.xmlAnalyst == null' if any missing analyst should recover from the stored row. The clarifying sentence is preferred since current behaviour is already correct.

findings.title: computePlayerAccuracyByScope home/away split happens inside the helper after idempotency pass-through
findings.where: design.md 'Overlap-scoped stored player_accuracy AND summary' section
findings.problem: computePlayerAccuracyByScope canonicalises once over the sets it is handed, then filters home/away internally on the already-canonical instances. The design asserts label parity at the 'both' level but does not explicitly state that the home/away sub-scope filtering runs inside the helper on the idempotency-preserved full-set labels. Correct as designed, just implicit.
findings.fix: Add one line noting computePlayerAccuracyByScope does its own home/away split internally on the preserved labels, so stored home/away match the live view's home/away and not merely both.
